reasons: Claimed status is 'compliant', and the redline is identical to the original paragraphs with no comment — correct behaviour for a compliant finding (no negotiation ask raised).

The cited text supports compliance: § 11 (p0084) makes fees payable only per the Fee Schedule for what is taken, with no minimum, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume-cap language binding the Customer (Sparkling).

p0065 shows maintenance on a renewable one-year term rather than a multi-year non-cancellable commitment, and p0118 gives Sparkling an at-will 90-day termination right, satisfying the rule's requirement that any commitment have an exit; this meets the preferred position.

Deterministic checks are empty and no detection keywords ('minimum', 'commit to purchase', 'take or pay', 'shortfall', volume caps) appear in the cited paragraphs, consistent with the compliance conclusion.

Residual risk noted but not disqualifying: the Fee Schedule itself is not reproduced, so a minimum commitment could in theory sit there; the rationale is otherwise accurate and appropriately scoped to the provided text.
